Looking at this problem, I need to determine whether a morphism of ringed spaces $(f,\theta):(X,\mathcal{O}_X)\to(Y,\mathcal{O}_Y)$ with $f$ a homeomorphism and $\theta$ an isomorphism of sheaves of rings is necessarily an isomorphism of ringed spaces.

**Answer: Yes, it is necessarily an isomorphism of ringed spaces.**

## Proof

Recall that a morphism of ringed spaces $(f,\theta):(X,\mathcal{O}_X)\to(Y,\mathcal{O}_Y)$ consists of a continuous map $f:X\to Y$ and a morphism of sheaves of rings $\theta:\mathcal{O}_Y\to f_*\mathcal{O}_X$. An isomorphism of ringed spaces is a morphism admitting a two-sided inverse morphism.

**Constructing the inverse.** Since $f$ is a homeomorphism, $g:=f^{-1}:Y\to X$ is a continuous map. We define a sheaf morphism $\phi:\mathcal{O}_X\to g_*\mathcal{O}_Y$ as follows. For each open set $U\subseteq X$, since $f$ is a homeomorphism, $f(U)$ is open in $Y$, and we have the isomorphism
$$\theta_{f(U)}:\mathcal{O}_Y(f(U))\to\mathcal{O}_X(f^{-1}(f(U)))=\mathcal{O}_X(U).$$
Since $\theta$ is an isomorphism of sheaves, each $\theta_{f(U)}$ is a ring isomorphism. Define
$$\phi_U:=\theta_{f(U)}^{-1}:\mathcal{O}_X(U)\to\mathcal{O}_Y(f(U))=\mathcal{O}_Y(g^{-1}(U))=(g_*\mathcal{O}_Y)(U).$$

**$\phi$ is a well-defined morphism of sheaves of rings.** We must verify compatibility with restriction. If $U'\subseteq U$ are open in $X$, then $f(U')\subseteq f(U)$ are open in $Y$. Since $\theta$ is a sheaf morphism, the diagram
$$\begin{array}{ccc}\mathcal{O}_Y(f(U)) & \xrightarrow{\theta_{f(U)}} & \mathcal{O}_X(U)\\ \downarrow & & \downarrow \\ \mathcal{O}_Y(f(U')) & \xrightarrow{\theta_{f(U')}} & \mathcal{O}_X(U')\end{array}$$
commutes. Taking inverses of the horizontal isomorphisms, the diagram with arrows reversed also commutes, which is exactly the compatibility condition for $\phi$. Each $\phi_U$ is a ring homomorphism (being the inverse of one), so $\phi$ is a morphism of sheaves of rings.

**Verifying the compositions are identities.** We check that $(g,\phi)\circ(f,\theta)=\mathrm{id}_{(X,\mathcal{O}_X)}$ and $(f,\theta)\circ(g,\phi)=\mathrm{id}_{(Y,\mathcal{O}_Y)}$.

*First composition* $(g,\phi)\circ(f,\theta):(X,\mathcal{O}_X)\to(X,\mathcal{O}_X)$: On topological spaces, $g\circ f=f^{-1}\circ f=\mathrm{id}_X$. On sheaves, the composed map $\mathcal{O}_X\to(g\circ f)_*\mathcal{O}_X=\mathcal{O}_X$ is, on each open $U\subseteq X$,
$$\mathcal{O}_X(U)\xrightarrow{\phi_U}\mathcal{O}_Y(f(U))\xrightarrow{(g_*\theta)_U}\mathcal{O}_X(U),$$
where $(g_*\theta)_U=\theta_{g^{-1}(U)}=\theta_{f(U)}$. This composition is $\theta_{f(U)}\circ\theta_{f(U)}^{-1}=\mathrm{id}_{\mathcal{O}_X(U)}$.

*Second composition* $(f,\theta)\circ(g,\phi):(Y,\mathcal{O}_Y)\to(Y,\mathcal{O}_Y)$: On topological spaces, $f\circ g=f\circ f^{-1}=\mathrm{id}_Y$. On sheaves, the composed map $\mathcal{O}_Y\to(f\circ g)_*\mathcal{O}_Y=\mathcal{O}_Y$ is, on each open $V\subseteq Y$,
$$\mathcal{O}_Y(V)\xrightarrow{\theta_V}\mathcal{O}_X(f^{-1}(V))\xrightarrow{(f_*\phi)_V}\mathcal{O}_Y(V),$$
where $(f_*\phi)_V=\phi_{f^{-1}(V)}=\theta_{f(f^{-1}(V))}^{-1}=\theta_V^{-1}$. This composition is $\theta_V^{-1}\circ\theta_V=\mathrm{id}_{\mathcal{O}_Y(V)}$.

Both compositions are identities, so $(g,\phi)$ is a two-sided inverse of $(f,\theta)$.

**Conclusion.** The morphism $(f,\theta)$ admits an inverse morphism of ringed spaces, hence is an isomorphism of ringed spaces. $\blacksquare$
